The page links 'VEP_Endbericht_Massnahmen und Handlungskonzept' (11.2 MB), whose title page reads 'Dortmund, im Februar 2024', and a Handlungskonzept PDF. Matches.

Opened the final report PDF (158 pages; title page 'Dortmund, im Februar 2024'). Measure D3.1 (pp. 86-88): 'ueber 7.000 Stellplaetzen', 'gerade einmal ungefaehr zur Haelfte belegt' in the peak hour, 'es gibt allerdings ein Verteilungsproblem'; recommends comprehensive parking management, raising on-street fees 'wie bereits Mitte 2022 angegangen' so on-street is dearer than collective facilities, further development of the Parkleitsystem, needs-based extension of resident parking, and medium to long term on-street spaces essentially only for delivery, disabled parking, car sharing, taxis, drop-off and in parts residents. All as drafted. (The figure is restated from the baseline analysis, which is fine.)

Same final report, section on Park&Ride (pp. 101-102): P+R should be set up primarily at SPNV stops in the surrounding area; per the RMV P+R plan, creating a basic P+R offer is to be checked at the stations Giessen-Licher Strasse and Giessen-Erdkauter Weg, and also for the Philosophenhoehe site; an effective P+R at the Giessener Ring requires ('zwingend') city-wide parking management with clearly higher fees, the largest possible removal of near-destination on-street spaces and possibly capacity limits. 'Fewer on-street spaces' is a mild paraphrase of 'weitestgehender Wegfall'. Worded as recommendation, correct.

Opened the baseline report PDF (128 pages; 'Dortmund, im November 2021'). Pp. 75-80: 'ueber 6.500 Parkplaetze in Parkhaeusern, Tiefgaragen oder bewirtschafteten Parkplaetzen' in the centre and nearby; 'eine Stunde Parken zwischen 0,50 EUR und 2 EUR'; garages on the Parkleitsystem examined in June 2020 for a normal weekday; maximum utilisation 50 percent between 12 and 13 h, over 1,700 free spaces; Selterstor 88 percent, Dern Passage 71 percent; conclusion 'kein Parkplatzmangel, sondern eher ein Verteilungsproblem'. Matches.

Same baseline report, p. 74-75: dynamic Parkleitsystem 'vor ueber 15 Jahren in Betrieb genommen und zuletzt hinsichtlich der Darstellung/Lesbarkeit und der Wegefuehrung als veraltet kritisiert'; in 2020 the Johannesstrasse car parks were integrated using individual detection and overhead sensors, two LED boards on both sides of the Suedanlage; use of the technology 'soll fuer weitere Parkbereiche geprueft werden'. Matches.

items.note: Opened jura.cc (law firm of Dr. Usebach, Koeln; 30 Aug 2023), which summarises Hess. VGH press release 16/2023 of 30.08.2023. Confirmed: Beschluss of 29 Aug 2023, 2 B 987/23, city's Beschwerde rejected; the city plans extensive changes on the Anlagenring, in particular a two-lane bicycle street; three traffic orders (Braugasse, Landgrafenstrasse, Senckenbergstrasse) of the first construction phase; two residents had won an Eilantrag at the Verwaltungsgericht Giessen; the court also points to the high traffic importance of the ring for car traffic and low cycling use. Wrong/too strong: 'no proven danger' - the court said the city had not 'plausibel dargelegt' the required danger or the special circumstances. The blog headline ('Rechtswidrigkeit ... bestaetigt') overstates an interim-relief decision; the draft text is more careful, but the summary's 'blocked' should be 'upheld an interim order against three first-phase orders'. Medium confidence is right (secondary source; court press release itself not opened by me).
items.corrected_text: On 29 August 2023 the Hessian administrative court of appeal (VGH, case 2 B 987/23) rejected the city's complaint against an urgent-application decision of the Gießen administrative court, which had gone in favour of two residents against three traffic orders (Braugasse, Landgrafenstraße, Senckenbergstraße) issued for the first phase of the city's Anlagenring traffic experiment; the experiment planned, among other changes, a two-lane bicycle street around the inner city. The court found that the city had not plausibly shown the danger to road safety or the special circumstances that such an experiment requires, and it noted the ring's high importance for car traffic against its currently low use by cyclists. This account is a law firm's summary (jura.cc, 30 August 2023) of the court's press release.

items.note: Opened the city notice PDF (3 pages). Confirmed: Magistrat invites interested companies to apply for special-use permits for e-charging points on public parking spaces; fees 0.50 euro per started kW per charge point and month up to 22 kW, 0.25 above 22 kW; 500 euros one-off for signage/marking and 150 euros processing per point; term up to 120 months; at most 15 sites (each up to 4 spaces); 'Richtlinie E-Ladesaeulen vom 1.9.2025' applies. Wrong/too strong: it is a city (Magistrat) guideline, the page does not call it a council guideline; and 17 November 2025, 12:00 is not a deadline to apply - applications can be made at any time, the date only fixes which applications count as simultaneous (lottery for competing sites). The notice itself carries no date (the 2025-09 date is the guideline date).
items.corrected_text: A city notice invites interested companies to apply for special-use permits to put charging points on public parking spaces, under the city's e-charging guideline (Richtlinie E-Ladesäulen) dated 1 September 2025. Applications can be made at any time; those received by 12:00 on 17 November 2025 are treated as received simultaneously, with a lottery for competing sites. The notice sets a fee of 0.50 euros per started kW per charge point per month up to 22 kW (0.25 above), a one-off 500 euros for signage and marking and 150 euros processing per point, a term of up to 120 months, and at most 15 sites per applicant. The notice itself is undated.

corrected_summary: Gießen's city centre and its immediate surroundings have over 6,500 spaces in garages, underground car parks and managed lots according to the 2021 baseline report for the city's transport development plan (VEP), which also found garage prices of 0.50 to 2 euros an hour, and the final VEP report (February 2024, adopted by the council on 6 June 2024) counts over 7,000 inner-city spaces, only about half occupied in the peak hour. Both describe a distribution problem rather than a shortage: in a June 2020 weekday analysis, garages on the Parkleitsystem peaked at 50 percent occupancy while Selterstor reached 88 percent. The final VEP report recommends making on-street parking dearer than garage parking, and the city's parking fee ordinance of 11 July 2024 sets 3.00 euros an hour in Zone I (inside the Anlagenring and around the station), above the 1.00 to 2.00 euros an hour shown for the garages on the city's current list; a resident permit costs 120 euros a year in six zones. Contipark operates the DB BahnPark garages at the station (2.00 euros an hour on the DB sheet against 1.70 on the city's list), APCOA operates Neustädter (1,060 spaces by its own text, 1,030 in its data field), and the city's list shows the Sparkasse garage closed from 1 August 2026 and, on 21 October 2026, a Parkleitsystem fault. In 2025 the city invited operators to apply for permits to put charging points on public parking spaces (the outcome was not found), and in August 2023 the Hessian administrative court of appeal rejected the city's complaint against an interim order that had stopped three first-phase traffic orders of its Anlagenring traffic experiment (known only from a law firm's summary of the court's press release).
